svg.title: macOS · Import from Device · browsing · 460×520
svg.desc: Mirrors Remote/ImportWindow.swift (browse phase) over Shared/ProjectTransferClient.swift. Phase 1 of the project-transfer feature: a whole project — 1 to 20 GB of DNGs, ProRes and notes — moved off a phone or an iPad onto this Mac over the local network, with no `.lapse` archive written on either side. Its OWN `Window` scene (id "import", File ▸ Import from Device…, ⌘⇧I), not a section in RemoteWindow: that window is pinned to 208×248 pt because Watch layout parity is its entire reason for existing, and a project list with sizes and a progress bar cannot live in a Watch canvas without wrecking the thing it exists to protect. `Window` rather than `WindowGroup` for the same reason the main window is one: the serving listener holds a SINGLE peer and replaces it on any new connection, so two import windows on one Mac would tear each other down. The browser is NWBrowser over `_letslapse-xfer._tcp` — a different service from the camera remote's `_letslapse-remote._tcp`, because serving a library and driving a shutter are different grants with different lifetimes, and a client browsing for one must never find the other. Plain NWParameters with includePeerToPeer and NO interface restriction, which is what makes a USB-tethered device appear here with no second transport and no extra code. The row's caption is model · project count (from the TXT record, so it can be said before anybody types a code) · and the interface, but ONLY when the answer is unambiguous: a device advertising on several interfaces at once cannot be labelled honestly, and how a tethered iOS device reports its InterfaceType is a device check rather than something to assume — so one interface gets "Wi-Fi" or "Cable" and anything else says nothing. `tools/transfer_probe.swift` prints the raw list for that check. A denied Local Network permission is called out in place of the empty state, because otherwise it is indistinguishable from "no devices on this network" — the single most confusing failure this link has. Verified 2026-08-27 against a simulator serving its library; staged with LL_TRANSFER=1 (the window is behind ⌘⇧I, which no headless run can press).
